messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

First request: net worth of Lionel Messi in Euros. So call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "Lionel Messi", currency "EUR".

Second: net worth of LeBron James in British Pounds. So call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "LeBron James", currency "GBP".

Third: BMI of person weighing 85 kg, height 180 cm, metric. So call calculate_bmi with weight 85, height 180, unit "metric". Actually default is metric, but we can specify.

Fourth: BMI of person weighing 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches, imperial. Need to convert weight to pounds? But optional unit param chooses between 'imperial' and 'metric'. So if unit is 'imperial', weight should be in pounds, height in inches? But the description says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. That seems contradictory. But likely the function expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters regardless of unit? But the unit param might adjust conversion internally. Let's assume weight in kilograms and height in centimeters always, but unit indicates how to interpret? Actually typical BMI calculation uses weight in kilograms and height in meters. If unit is imperial, weight in pounds, height in inches. So we need to provide weight in pounds and height in inches. But the function signature says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. But maybe it's just a mistake. We can still pass weight in kilograms and height in centimeters, but set unit to 'imperial'? That wouldn't make sense. Let's interpret that the function expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters regardless of unit param. But the unit param might be used to convert from imperial to metric before calculation. So we should provide weight in kilograms and height in centimeters even if unit is imperial? But then why pass unit? Might be used to indicate that the input values are in imperial units. So we should provide weight in pounds and height in inches. But the signature says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. This is ambiguous. However, the user explicitly wants BMI using imperial system. So we should pass weight in pounds and height in inches, and unit 'imperial'.

Thus for the fourth request: weight 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches. Convert height to inches: 6 ft *12 =72 +2=74 inches. So call calculate_bmi with weight 200, height 74, unit 'imperial'.
